extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing
extraction.description: VoiceAssistant-Eval is a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, spoken dialogue, multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and heterogeneous images. The benchmark evaluates 21 open-source models and GPT-4o-Audio on content quality, speech quality, and consistency.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.citeAs: Wang, K., Ren, H., Lu, Z., Zhan, M., & Li, H. (2025). VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.22651.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from 37 source datasets including natural sounds, music, dialogue, and images. For voice personalization, texts from RoleBench were used with 100 distinct roles and three representative audio clips per role. Speech instructions were synthesized using three TTS models (F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B) and evaluated with UTMOS, regenerating clips with scores below 3.8. Synthesized audio was transcribed with Whisper and compared to original instructions, retaining recordings with lowest word error rates.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source datasets include 23 audio understanding datasets (e.g., LibriSpeech, Common Voice, Clotho, AudioCaps, MusicCaps, AIR-Bench) for listening; 22 datasets (e.g., RoleBench, AlpacaEval, MT-Bench-101, BeaverTails-Eval, SD-Eval, VocalBench) for speaking; and MMMU for viewing.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Multi-stage curation: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance; (2) Validation excluding incomplete or inappropriate items (corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, incorrect answers) removing ~10% of candidates; (3) Categorization into 13 task categories based on source metadata; (4) Balanced sampling to equalize category representation, resulting in 10,497 samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were derived from source datasets. For role-play, 100 roles were selected with three audio clips per role. Speech synthesis used three TTS models with quality checks (UTMOS >3.8) and transcription verification (Whisper). Evaluation uses gpt-oss-20b with thirteen evaluator prompts for content quality, emotion2vec for emotion, UTMOS for speech quality, and Whisper for consistency.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B, Whisper-Large-v3, UTMOS, emotion2vec, gpt-oss-20b
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation validation showed high correlation (0.92) and agreement rate (96.1%) between automated scoring and human judgments. Stability analysis over ten runs showed low variance. Statistical significance testing confirmed performance differences.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B, Whisper-Large-v3, UTMOS, emotion2vec, gpt-oss-20b, Wespeaker
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Code and data will be released at the project page. The dataset is under MIT license. The authors will maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal, and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender, age, emotion, language, culture, experience (via role-play and emotion tasks)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark includes safety alignment evaluation and identifies gaps in robustness and safety. It provides safety cards describing acceptable use, known risks, and red-team tests for voice cloning abuse. The authors prohibit training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential biases from source data and design choices: role-play subset uses fixed 100 roles which may encode stereotypes; monolingual focus (English) may not capture global variability; questions drawn from academic/synthetic sources may not reflect real deployments.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limited diversity (monolingual English, fixed roles), limited model evaluation (only one proprietary model), reliance on automated measures and GPT-based scoring (may introduce noise/bias), offline static evaluation (does not measure latency, partial utterances, barge-in, error recovery), gaps in task coverage (no video-audio integration or continuous streaming).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning; intended for evaluating voice assistants on listening, speaking, and viewing tasks; not for training models for cheating or impersonation without consent.
